## Findings
- claim-1: Inspected alternate-provider full text: ar5iv’s rendering of St. Dizier–Yong, DOI 10.1112/jlms.12832, supplied with SHA-256 `6066dee1db75213a13ca9c407c8944c09c7391fb0fb69f1d4a386ed4292fc456`. It identifies the 2011 Reiner–Woo–Yong paper separately as reference [12]. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 548-550]
- claim-2: The supplied rendering contains visibly corrupted required material: after introducing (8) and (9), it truncates mathematical content, and Definition 2.1 reads only “valid if \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\) with \(r\ 9)\),” omitting its inequalities. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 149-164]
- claim-3: The visible linkage is: Lemma 2.5 says a specified nonzero homogeneous syzygy implies consistency of decomposable equations (10); Theorem 4.4 declares the corresponding system inconsistent when wide right sides vanish and some tall right side is nonzero; Theorem 4.5 invokes Lemma 2.5 and Theorem 4.4. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 176-190] [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-502]
- claim-4: In Theorem 4.4, “\(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\)” is proof-case-specific, not a theorem hypothesis: the theorem begins “For any valid \(\varphi\),” and its proof subsequently treats both \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\) and \(N>\min(j,n-r-i)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-486]
- claim-5: The requested source certificate is **not established** from the supplied record: the only alternate-provider full text is corrupted precisely where complete equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1’s valid-tuple inequalities are required. Hence neither the visible linkage nor adjacent 2011-paper identification can substitute for one uncorrupted bounded source-29 excerpt.
## Strategy
Compare only source-29’s supplied ar5iv full text (SHA-256 `6066dee1db75213a13ca9c407c8944c09c7391fb0fb69f1d4a386ed4292fc456`) against the required certificate elements and distinguish visible theorem text from proof-local case splits.

## Gaps
The sole recorded full-text provider is corrupted at equations (8)–(10) and Definition 2.1 [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 149-164, 176-186]. No different provider, uncorrupted bounded extraction, or complete valid-tuple inequalities are supplied. Thus full hypothesis classification is impossible. Only the visible split \(N\le\min(j,n-r-i)\) is identifiable as proof-local, since Theorem 4.4 instead assumes any valid tuple [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 473-486].

The requested source certificate is **not established**. The adjacent 2011 reference and truncated linkage do not substitute for it.

## Next
Obtain a hashed alternate-provider source-29 excerpt with stable locators preserving complete equations (8)–(10), Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.5, and Theorems 4.4–4.5.
